To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the galactosyllated PLGA surface enhanced the liver‐specific functional activity and cell–cell and cell–matrix interactions of HLCs.
the galactosilated PLGA enhanced the cellular behaviour of HLCs, including proliferation, aggregation, albumin secretion and gap junction formation.
galactosyl‐PLGA promoted the proliferation, aggregation, and hepatic functional differentiation of MSCs.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a novel galactosyl‐functionalized polymer for the fabrication of a bioartificial liver (BAL).
the development of a galactosyl‐PLGA scaffold for hepatic tissue engineering.
the development of a novel method of producing galactosyl‐PLGA, and its potential application in the field of tissue engineering.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the galactosilated PLGA surface enhanced the liver‐specific function of HLCs, and the results of this study suggest that the galactylated PLGA surface is a promising biomaterial for hepatic tissue engineering.
the galactosilated PLGA scaffold can be a promising candidate for liver tissue engineering.
galactosyl‐PLGA is a suitable scaffold material for hepatic tissue engineering.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we developed a novel method for surface modification using ICP‐CVD, which is a simple, fast and cost‐effective technique.
the galactosamine‐functionalized PLGA surface could be a promising scaffold for hepatocyte culture.

the galactosamine‐functionalized PLGA surface is a promising candidate for hepatic tissue engineering and the galactosaminated PLGA surface could be used to improve cell–cell and cell–matrix interactions of the HLCs.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the galactosilated PLGA surface could enhance the proliferation and differentiation of HLCs, and also improve the cell–cell interactions of HLCs.
the galactosamine‐modified PLGA surface is able to enhance HLC proliferation and differentiation and the formation of cell–cell interactions.
the surface modification of PLGA using galactose‐containing molecules can enhance the cellular behaviours of HLCs.
